machine: Flash (Vinay's Ubuntu box, ssh flash, 12 threads, qwen-test venv: python 3.14 + numpy 2.5.4 + tokenizers 0.23.3)

model_pair.local_note: pair already present on Flash from the pre-hackathon Signet work; no download was needed
model_pair.matrices: embedding + 32 blocks x (attn.q/k/v/o_proj, mlp.gate/up/down_proj) = 225 delta matrices

probe_set.source: the combined 96 fresh Spark probe items from Phase 1 (original 24 held-out + 72 expansion items); neither the Qwen sweep nor this pair's sweep saw them during search, Stage 1, or Stage 2

byte_matched_variant.name: o-down-rebalanced
byte_matched_variant.reason: Lowered down/gate/up proportionally while keeping o_proj highest to shed rank cost under budget.

price_validation.method: factored.storage_bytes summed over the 225 real matrices read from the model files, computed in the Flash build pass (same code path as Stage 2 pricing)

method.configs: base (no delta), full_delta (Instruct weights), and factored_delta per recipe: uniform_rank32, the Stage 2 winner, and the byte-matched variant
method.scoring: identical to second_pair Stage 2: ChatML prompt (system line 'You are a helpful assistant.'); target logprob = summed log-probability of the answer tokens; accuracy = first-token accuracy; gap_closed = (factored - base) / (full - base) on mean target logprob, per subset with that subset's own base/full references
method.forward_pass: the second_pair_stage2 NumPy SmolLM2 forward, validated in Stage 2 against the prior Signet run's published bucket means

verdict.byte_fair_headline_question: does o-down-rebalanced beat uniform_rank32 on the combined 96 fresh items?
